JP Morgan analysed 260,000 bank accounts over three years to find out exactly how lucrative working for companies such as Uber and Airbnb can be

This is useful data for economists and policy makers, but it's silly to say things like this based on it:

The report concluded that participating in the sharing economy is a "far better option" to boost earnings during a work slump if the alternatives are to spend less or take out additional loans.

What people need to know is not only the amount they can make doing this kind of work, but the costs per dollar earned.

How much time, gasoline and wear and tear on your vehicle does it cost per dollar earned as an Uber driver?

How much time, materials, repairs and stress does it cost per dollar earned renting something out on AirBnB?

If these are your only way of making extra cash and you desperately need it, you're not very concerned about time. If you're not so desperate or you have other options, you need to know all of the costs.

I've wondered if people have looked hard at the long term cost of car upkeep and maintenence although it seems now a days most people don't even think about it outside of an oil change and gas.

Years ago when I was still in high school I thought about getting a gig as a pizza delivery person opted out after looking into the upkeep on my car at the time. It just wasn't worth it even if the tips were great.
